description: This CEPAL study sets out the core concepts of infrastructure resilience and the main obstacles to building it in Latin America and the Caribbean, arguing for an integrated approach that balances resilience, efficiency and sustainability under the 2030 Agenda. Fabio Weikert Bicalho of the Infrastructure Services Unit of CEPAL's International Trade and Integration Division wrote it, published in 2021 as number 160 of the International Trade series (LC/TS.2020/177), with input from the World Bank's Jun Rentschler among others. Using the COVID-19 pandemic and the region's infrastructure gap as context, it analyses what limits the capacity of transport, connectivity and utility networks and their users to respond to and recover from hazards, and closes with policy considerations on trade-offs between resilience and efficiency. Coverage is Latin America and the Caribbean. Format and access: an 83-page Spanish PDF, here the copy in the EU-LAC Foundation digital library. Licence: United Nations copyright; free to read. Caveats: it is a policy analysis that reuses published figures, not new data. It frames resilience and capacity planning studies of infrastructure services in the region. A related catalogue record is CEPAL's report on cyber attacks on logistics and critical infrastructure.
